biography.plain_text: Hugh D. Fuller Jr. is a racing driver whose career moved from endurance cars to offshore powerboats. He competed at Daytona and Sebring in the 1990s, then became a national and world champion on the water. Fuller set an offshore Super Cat speed record and continued racing in UIM Class 1 competition into 2023.

long_biography.plain_text:
An Alabama native, Hugh D. Fuller Jr. first built a competitive career in sports-car racing. He entered IMSA events with HDF Motorsports and contested major endurance fixtures including the 24 Hours of Daytona and 12 Hours of Sebring. The experience established a disciplined approach to speed, vehicle control and preparation that later carried onto the water.

Fuller moved into offshore powerboat competition around 2000, racing with experienced throttlemen such as Jerry Gilbreath, John Tomlinson and Rich Wyatt. He collected national and world titles across Super Cat, Extreme and Unlimited classes and earned a place in the American Power Boat Association's Hall of Champions. His career has remained unusually durable. International records credit him with a Super Cat speed mark, while UIM results still listed him as a Class 1 driver in 2023.
